# The Lights That Answer the Long Wait

## Scripture

*"But do not forget this one thing, dear friends: With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day. The Lord is not slow in keeping his promise, as some understand slowness."* — 2 Peter 3:8–9a (NIV)

## Reflection

Every October, the Orionid meteor shower returns. These fleeting streaks of light are debris from Halley's Comet—dust shed decades ago, meeting our atmosphere right on schedule. Astronomers don't wonder *if* the Orionids will appear. They know. The comet left its trail, and Earth crosses it faithfully, year after year.

There is something deeply comforting about a sky that keeps its appointments. We live in a world of broken promises and delayed hopes, where waiting often feels like abandonment. Yet God built a universe where even ancient dust arrives on time.

Peter reminds us that God's timing is not our timing. What feels like delay to us may be, from His vantage, a single day. The Orionids teach us that long waits do not mean forgotten promises. Halley's Comet won't return until 2061—but its dust still lights our skies every year, proof that what was set in motion long ago still arrives exactly when it should.

If you are waiting on God today—for an answer, a healing, a breakthrough—take heart. His promises are not lost in the dark. They travel toward you with certainty, and they will not miss their appointed hour. The God who scheduled the meteor showers has not forgotten you.

## Prayer

Lord, when waiting feels endless, remind me that Your timing is perfect. The heavens keep their appointments because You are faithful. Help me trust that Your promises will arrive—not late, but right on time. Amen.
